name: xero-contact-to-notion-company

trigger.authentication_note: The work.flowers Xero connection — the same one bound as the `xero_wf` alias, which the manual sweep still uses.
trigger.params_note: `organization` is the work.flowers tenant. `_zap_polling_interval_minutes` is an UNDOCUMENTED Zapier key, offered by Zapier support on 2026-11-04 as a 'temporary workaround'; without it a durable poller runs ~1/min (~1,440 Xero calls/day against the tenant's 5,000). Verified 2026-11-04 on a Drive poller (15 → polls 15–17 min apart, files batched per poll). It must be a NUMBER. scripts/publish-changed-zaps.mjs refuses a Xero polling trigger without it. If Zapier ever drops support, the fallback is the schedule trigger this replaced (git history, before PR for 2026-11).
trigger.cadence_note: Polls every 15 minutes since 2026-11 (~96 Xero calls/day, the classic Zap's old rate). Was a daily 6:30 AM schedule (2026-10-31) and hourly before that, sweeping a 7-day window. Polls that find nothing cost no Zapier task; each updated contact is one run (≥1 task from 2026-12-01) — ~12 contacts per 13 days observed, so about the same task count as the daily schedule, with links landing in ≤15 min instead of ≤1 day.
trigger.dedupe_note: The main case is a contact created by hand and given its Account Number LATER — an UPDATE to a contact that already fired once. That only reaches us if Zapier re-fires `updated_contact` for an already-seen ContactID (bug W6ZE93-VMEWP, fixed for durable app triggers 2026-10-28 but never tested on Xero). Verify after cutover by setting an Account Number on an existing contact; if it does not fire, revert to the schedule.
trigger.manual_run_note: `trigger-workflow 019fdb77-594e-7426-a1f2-9c0b153d986c --input '{"sweep":true,"dryRun":true}'` runs the old 7-day sweep and reports what it WOULD write, writing nothing; drop dryRun to apply it. Use after an outage or if a link was missed. An empty `{}` now THROWS rather than sweeping — the poller never sends one.

connections_note: notion_wf is the work.flowers workspace connection. NEVER bind the Knoxx connection (02b95b31-c152-8800-9036-1107e08f70da) — it points at a client workspace and cannot see work.flowers databases.

purpose.direction: XERO -> NOTION. The complement of xero-contact-from-notion-deal, which covers Notion -> Xero.
purpose.the_case: A contact is created in Xero by other means — typically a transaction arrives from a new vendor and the contact is made by hand. If a Company record already exists in Notion, its Notion Company ID (the `ID` property, e.g. COM-766) is pasted into that Xero contact's ACCOUNT NUMBER, and this workflow completes the link. Nothing changes on the Notion side, so no Notion webhook fires and the other durable never runs — which is why this cannot be folded into it.

titles: Add Xero Contact ID to Company IDs Table
Associate Xero Contact with Notion Company
replaces_classic_zaps.they_were_duplicates: Functionally identical: same trigger (XeroCLIAPI@2.21.0 / updated_contact), connection, organization, filter, table, lookup and write fields. Differences were cosmetic only — titles, the per-Zap step ids inside their gives[...] references, a stepTitle on one filter, and _zap_search_success_on_miss being the string "False" in one vs boolean false in the other.
replaces_classic_zaps.cost: ~2,880 Xero API calls/day between them at 1-minute polling — the largest single contributor to the 2026-08-06 quota exhaustion, and the part the durable pollers alone never explained. Moved to 15-minute polling (~192/day) on 2026-08-07, then superseded by this workflow (~24/day).
replaces_classic_zaps.the_bug_they_had: They wrote the ContactID into [Table] Company IDs (f15) and left the Notion property empty. (1) THE LINK WAS TEMPORARY: notion-companies-to-zapier-table is a true mirror — its source comment reads 'empty in Notion clears the table value' — and `Xero Contact ID` is in its mirrored set, so the next edit of that company wiped f15 back out. (2) THE OTHER DURABLE'S DEDUPE GUARD STAYED BLIND: it reads `Xero Contact ID` off the Notion page, so a later Companies-button or Deals-stage trigger would re-run the upsert, and Xero matches contacts on NAME — silently overwriting the hand-made vendor contact's people.
replaces_classic_zaps.action_required: TURN BOTH OFF in the Zapier UI. While enabled they keep writing f15 directly (reintroducing the temporary-link bug) and keep costing ~192 Xero calls/day. Classic Zaps are exposed by neither the SDK CLI nor the MCP connector, so this is not machine-verifiable from here.

why_schedule_not_polling_2026_08: HISTORICAL (superseded 2026-11 by _zap_polling_interval_minutes — see trigger.params_note). Migrating `updated_contact` as a POLLING durable would have been WORSE than the classic Zap: a durable trigger has no polling-interval field (the --trigger payload accepts only selected_api / action / authentication_id / params, verified across all 43 live triggers in the account), so it would run at the account default — ~1,440 Xero calls/day versus the 96/day the classic Zap cost at its 15-minute override. A schedule trigger costs Xero nothing and puts the rate under our control: ~24/day.

company_ids.name: [Table] Company IDs
company_ids.role: Read here as the company lookup, and NOT merely as a gate: it is the ONLY source of the Notion page UUID. The Xero contact carries Notion's `ID` property (COM-766), not a UUID, so a Notion write is impossible without resolving it. Reads are free.

fields_used.Notion Page ID (f14): the page UUID written to — unobtainable from the Xero side
fields_used.Xero Contact ID (f15): the already-linked / conflict check, and the cache warmed after the Notion write

company_ids.why_it_is_also_written: After the authoritative Notion write, f15 is set in the same run. NOT a second source of truth — the mirror would set it anyway from the value just written to Notion. It exists only so the already-linked gate closes on THIS run instead of waiting on a webhook we do not control; without it a fire inside the mirror's latency window would re-issue an identical, harmless but pointless Notion PATCH. Writing ONLY here is what the classic Zaps did, and is the bug above.

safety.changed_link_never_applied: If the Notion company already carries a DIFFERENT Xero contact id, the workflow changes nothing and reports a conflict with a WARNING naming both ids. Either two Xero contacts claim the same company or an Account Number is wrong; both need a human, and silently repointing the link would hide it. The classic Zap's `f15 isnull` filter declined this case too, but silently.
safety.blast_radius: A poll run writes at most one link. MAX_LINKS_PER_RUN (25) caps Notion writes per manual sweep; nothing is lost when it trips — re-run the sweep.
safety.self_healing: No longer automatic: a poll run that fails is not retried by a later poll. Recovery is the manual {"sweep":true} run, which re-reads 7 days of UpdatedDateUTC.

determinism_note: The body runs in GUARDED mode, where `Date` is a Proxy whose construct trap throws DeterminismViolation BEFORE inspecting its arguments — so even a deterministic `new Date(Date.UTC(y,m,d))` is rejected as hard as a clock read. All date arithmetic is integer maths; the ONLY clock read is inside ctx.step("today"). Verified by grep before publish.
description: Xero New or Updated Contact poller (every 15 min) -> if the contact carries an Account Number, resolve it against [Table] Company IDs on Notion Company ID -> if the company has no Xero Contact ID yet, PATCH it onto the Notion Company page and warm the Table's copy. Declines a changed link rather than applying it. Replaces two functionally identical classic Zaps that wrote to the Table instead of Notion.

version_history.note: Initial version. Migrates two classic Zaps into one schedule-driven durable and fixes their write target (Notion, not the Table) — see replaces_classic_zaps. Validated before publish: tsc clean on first pass; determinism grep clean (single Date.now() inside ctx.step("today")); every write reachable only past the dryRun guard; per-item step names index-based off a batch sorted by ContactID, with the batch memoized by the fetch step so a retry cannot re-map an index. DRY RUN against live Xero and the real Table: window UpdatedDateUTC>=2026-07-31, 11 contacts read, 1 page, coverageIncomplete false, 5 candidates (COM-15, COM-318, COM-689, COM-766, COM-803), all 5 correctly `already linked` with their stored f15 matching the Xero ContactID exactly, 0 conflicts — which also confirms the classic Zap had been doing its job. Verified after publish: triggers[0].status active, enabled true, is_private FALSE (repo rule 8), both connections bound, deployed source byte-identical to the repo. THE WRITE PATH IS NOT YET EXERCISED — nothing currently needs linking. It is byte-identical to the proven implementation in xero-contact-from-notion-deal (same API version, connection, property name, payload shape) and notion-companies-to-zapier-table independently confirms `Xero Contact ID` is a rich_text property, but watch the first real link.

pending_verification: No contact has yet been linked by this workflow, because all 5 current candidates were already linked. To exercise the write path deliberately: create or pick a Xero contact whose Account Number is a Notion Company ID whose company has an EMPTY `Xero Contact ID`, then run with `{"dryRun":true}` first and confirm it reports `would link`. Watch for: `linked` non-empty with outcome `linked`; the Notion Company page's `Xero Contact ID` populated; f15 populated in the Table; and on the NEXT fire the same contact reported as `already linked`.
